immunofluorescent staining of renal biopsies from 15 patients with systemic sclerosis (SS), 10 with systemic lupus erythematosis (SLE), 2 with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and 3 with mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) was studied with antisera to IgA, IgG, IgM, fibrin, human renal glomerular basement membrane (GBM), and C3.
(1) IgG and C3 deposits were present in 11 of 14 patients with systemic lupus erythematous and 6 of 10 patients with scleroderma.

immunohistological studies with antisera against IgG, fibrin, C3, human renal glomerular basement membranes, and normal human kidney sections showed that immune deposits are present in the glomeruli of patients with systemic sclerosis and that these deposits are similar to those found in the kidneys of patients with systemic lupus erythematosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the immune system in the pathogenesis and progression of systemic lupus eryhematosus (S.E.E.) and systemic sclerosis.
the immunopathological aspects of systemic lupus erythematosis (SLE) and systemic sclerosis (SS), two diseases in which the kidneys are frequently involved.
the role of immunity as an aetiological factor in the pathogenesis and progression of renal disease in SLE and SS.

GBM antiserum was useful in demonstrating the deposition of immunoreactive material in glomeruli of diabetic patients, but the material was not immunoglobulin.

there is a close correlation between the deposition of immunoreactants and the presence of GBM antibodies in diabetic glomerulopathy but that the correlation between GBM antibodies and the deposition of immunocomplexes is not as clear.
the GBM antisera were of value for the demonstration of GBM, but were not helpful in elucidating the pathogenesis of the various renal diseases studied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in both SLE and SS there is a close relationship between the presence of immunoglobulains in glomeruli and the deposition of GBM antigens in the same glomeruli, and that the deposition of GBMs in glomeruli is not a feature of normal kidneys.
GBM antisera are not useful in the diagnosis of SLE or SS.
in SLE the GBM antiserum is a very sensitive marker for IgG and C3 deposits, whereas in SS it is a very sensitive and specific marker for IgG.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system plays a role in systemic lupus and systemic sclerosis.
there are some similarities in the immune complex deposits between the two diseases, but there are also some important differences.
there are no specific markers that can be used to diagnose SLE or SS.
